bridge: Builds on B01 DOM insertion, W01 request tracing and N06 responses. Use local text examples and the designated training labs only.
teaching:
Cross-site scripting confuses untrusted content with executable page behaviour. Reflected content comes back in an immediate response; stored content is retained and later shown; DOM-based faults arise in client-side source-to-sink flows. The location of storage is different from the parsing context that causes execution.

Output handling must match context. Plain text belongs in a text node or textContent. HTML attributes, JavaScript and URLs have different interpretation rules. A single generic escaping function cannot safely authorise every destination. If rich HTML is required, use a maintained sanitiser with a deliberate allowed-content policy.

Content Security Policy can reduce consequences but does not replace correct data handling. HttpOnly cookies restrict direct script reading of those cookies, yet an injected script may still act in the user's origin. Focus your evidence on where untrusted data crosses into an interpreting sink and verify the actual repair with harmless markers.
example: Local B01 page: input value: practice Safe sink: result.textContent = value Expected DOM: literal text, no child b element Stored variant: save the same text as a note; reload and render with textContent. The storage step changes persistence, not the safe insertion rule.
explanation: The marker is markup-shaped text, not an attack script. It lets you distinguish literal insertion from HTML parsing. A note stored safely in the database can still become dangerous if a later view inserts it into an executable context.
exercise: Use your local greeting page. Display the exact marker with textContent, inspect the node and record its child-element count. Repeat after saving/restoring the string as local practice data. Explain reflected versus stored handling.
solution: The marker remains literal and creates zero child elements in the result node. Persistence does not itself sanitise content. Evidence should identify the specific sink used on each rendering path.
challenge: An app safely renders a note in its main view but builds an inline script from the same note in an export preview. Explain why the first repair does not prove the preview safe and propose a design avoiding the script context.
challenge_solution: Each sink needs independent context analysis. Keep data out of inline executable source, pass it through a structured data channel and render plain text with DOM text APIs. Test both views with harmless delimiter/markup-shaped inputs.
